content:
ashwin: morning — seeing a sudden spike in ECONNRESET and broken pipe errors from model-serving in eu-west2 gpupool. Envoy logs show a lot of conntrack/NAT failures around the same time. Anyone else seeing this?

ryan: yep, health checks fired for several replicas in gpupool-eu-west2. Pod restarts up ~12% in the last 10m. digging into node metrics now.

maria: @oncall-bot opened an incident? :eyes:

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-412 (P2) — "eu-west2 gpupool NAT/conntrack saturation". Follow runbook: infra/conntrack.

ivan: checked a few affected hosts. `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` shows ~65534 and `nf_conntrack_max` is 65536. Kernel reports near-full conntrack table on d-ax-003 and d-ax-004.

ashwin: 65536 is the default on our images. Need mitigation immediately. Options: bump nf_conntrack_max, apply pod routing exceptions to avoid SNAT, or try to reduce churn. Thoughts?

laura: quick mitigation: we can sysctl bump it temporarily. longer term, we should avoid SNAT for east-west pod traffic (hairpin) — looks like kube-proxy MASQUERADE is catching intra-cluster calls when endpoints aren't flagged local.

ryan: doing a quick sysctl on the 10 most affected nodes now to buy time:
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
```
I'll roll as a one-off before we push a DaemonSet. Watch kernel memory usage.

maya: can we push the change via a privileged DaemonSet so we don't have to manual patch nodes? I'll prepare one if the manual change stabilizes things.

ivan: also seeing a huge number of sockets in TIME_WAIT and CLOSE_WAIT from sidecar proxies — looks like aggressive short-lived connections from prefetch or batch clients. That multiplies conntrack entries.

ashwin: could that be the prefetcher hitting model endpoints repeatedly (many small requests) so every request creates a new TCP tuple? If so we need to either reuse connections or enable keepalive.

laura: repro attempt: on a test node I forced traffic that should be local, but kube-proxy iptables MASQUERADE path was used because endpoints were not in the local loadbalancer set. So traffic left node and got SNATed — that's creating conntrack entries.

ryan: after bumping nf_conntrack_max on the 8 worst nodes, conntrack_count dropped to ~40k as the kernel sweeper reclaimed entries. Pod restarts dropped back to baseline. But this recurs after load spikes.

maria: early RCA hypotheses: (1) hairpin/SNAT for intra-cluster grpc causing large churn; (2) connection reuse not enabled in prefetch clients; (3) conntrack sizing/hash tuning suboptimal for GPU pool traffic patterns.

ivan: mitigation plan:
- short: deploy privileged DaemonSet to set nf_conntrack_max=262144 across all gpupool nodes and enable aggressive conntrack timeout reaping.
- medium: audit kube-proxy MASQUERADE rules for gpupool namespaces and add an exclusion for pod CIDR to avoid SNAT for pod-to-pod.
- long: evaluate CNI change or hostNetwork options for model workers + tune envoy/sidecar keepalive and connection pool settings.

ashwin: creating tickets for each. Also flagging potential memory impact of bigger conntrack tables — monitor node kernel memory under pressure.

maria: I'll update the runbook with the commands we used and add alert thresholds for nf_conntrack_count > 70% and pod restart spikes in gpupool.

ryan: note on costs — no extra instances spun up, but we did see slight latency increase during sweeps while connections were being reaped. Keep an eye on SLOs.

ivan: for the kernel-level follow-up, recommend we bump hashsize and consider newer kernel where nf_conntrack scales better under high ephemeral port churn.

laura: +1 to testing a no-SNAT patch for gpupool traffic in staging. I'll prototype iptables exception and report back.

ashwin: thanks team. Once runbook + tickets exist, I'll mark this thread resolved. :thumbsup:
